description:
Intent i002 (tcp-optwalk-len2, snapshot s01) complete. Four credible variants of the seed mechanism (missing remaining>=2 guard between the TCP kind byte and the length byte) found in snapshots/s01, all with literal in-range source quotes verified programmatically:

1. s01:net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:3713-3728 (HIGH) - tcp_parse_options() default path: 'opsize = *ptr++' at 3724 is executed after consuming the kind byte at 3714 with no 'if (length < 2) return;' between them; the opsize<2/opsize>length checks at 3725/3727 run after the fetch. When length==1 the loop reads one byte past the TCP option area. This is the pre-9609dad263f8 shape that the seed commit 07718be26568 itself cites as its inspiration; callers verified across tcp_input.c:5521/3855/6252, tcp_minisocks.c:100/593, and both syncookie paths (remote attacker-controlled bytes; tcp_v4_rcv pskb_may_pulls th->doff*4 so the option area bounds the read).

2. s01:net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:3875-3888 (MEDIUM) - tcp_parse_md5sig_option() has the identical unguarded kind->length sequence at 3886; the initial length<TCPOLEN_MD5SIG shortcut (3872) does not prevent length==1 on later iterations.

3. s01:net/netfilter/nf_synproxy_core.c:42-56 (HIGH) - synproxy_parse_options() into a fixed 'u8 buf[40]' stack buffer: 'opsize = *ptr++' at 53 with no length<2 guard; when the final option byte is a single non-EOL/non-NOP kind (doff=15, length=40) the loop reads buf[40], one byte past the 40-byte on-stack array (KASAN stack OOB). Sibling netfilter walks in the same tree (nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c:398/459) DO have the guard, proving the divergence.

4. s01:net/netfilter/xt_tcpmss.c:67-70 (MEDIUM) - tcpmss_mt() reads op[i+1] at 70 when op[i]>=2 without an i+1<optlen bound ('for (i = 0; i < optlen; )'), reading _opt[40] past the 40-byte stack buffer or uninitialized stack beyond the copied region.

Safe (guard present or walk bounded): dccp_parse_options (net/dccp/options.c:79 explicit opt_ptr==opt_end check), nf_conntrack_proto_tcp tcp_options/tcp_sack, nf_conntrack_seqadj, xt_TCPMSS, xt_TCPOPTSTRIP, nft_exthdr (all optlen() helpers invoked with >=1 byte margin), xt_tcpudp, tcp_repair_options_est, and both syncookies.c files (delegate to tcp_parse_options).

Limitations: findings are line-verified structural matches only - no KASAN reproducer was built (read-only tree, no build config); the over-read byte gates parse decisions rather than being echoed to the attacker; synproxy/xt_tcpmss need their modules loaded and rules referencing them; tcp_parse_md5sig_option needs CONFIG_TCP_MD5SIG. net/mptcp, tcp_parse_mss_option, tcp_ao.c, and bpf_search_tcp_opt do not exist in this snapshot. Non-TCP parser classes were out of scope (covered by sibling intents i005-i013).
